summary.headline: Orders and revenue both beat target and the quarter is ahead, but the year is still behind at 94.5% of target with the required pace above recent levels.

points.what: Orders came in at 104.1% of the weekly target and revenue at 116.6%, with revenue of $67,572.
points.so_what: Revenue cleared its target by a wider margin than orders did, so the week's beat does not rest on volume alone.

points.what: Orders reached 889, outside their 8-week range, and were up 71.6% on last year.
points.so_what: Order growth sits just below the 75% year-on-year growth the targets assume, while revenue growth of 90.5% is above it.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 108.3% of target after two weeks of Q2.
points.so_what: The quarter has opened with a buffer, unlike the three completed months before it.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue stands at 94.5% of target while the quarter is ahead.
points.so_what: The year and the quarter point in opposite directions, so weekly beats have to be read against the annual position.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $49,135 below target, with January, February and March all closing behind.
points.so_what: Three completed months behind target set the size of the shortfall the rest of the year has to absorb.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 rose 2.2 pp to 11.5%, a notable move rated bad both week on week and against last year.
points.so_what: This is the clearest deterioration in order quality in a week that otherwise beat target.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.9 pp to 15.1%, rated bad, and one percentage point is worth $796 of revenue.
points.so_what: A larger share of the week's orders is being taken out of gross revenue than in the prior week.

points.what: Orders finished 35 above the weekly target and revenue $9,614 above it.
points.so_what: The week added to the quarter's position rather than drawing down on it.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $128,119 leaves $755,967 of the full-quarter target across 11 remaining weeks.
points.so_what: Almost the whole quarter is still outstanding despite the ahead-of-target start.

points.what: Reaching the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $80,135 of revenue a week, against a recent 8-week pace of $60,216.
points.so_what: The required pace sits well above anything achieved recently, which puts the full-year target out of reach at this rate.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 36.9% and contributed 41 orders, 107.9% of the week's total change.
points.so_what: One region accounted for more than the entire increase, with APAC and North America both below last week.

points.what: Facebook added 15 orders, 39.5% of the week's change, on growth of 31.2%.
points.so_what: Search was flat week on week, so the order gain came from outside the largest source.

points.what: Display orders rose 41.7% to 51 and were up 292.3% on last year.
points.so_what: The smallest source is growing far faster than the 75% year-on-year growth the targets assume.

points.what: AOV reached $89.50, up 7.9% on last week and 9.3% on last year, both rated good.
points.so_what: Revenue grew faster than orders this week, and order value is what separates the two.

points.what: The cancellation rate of 15.1% is 1.3 pp below the same week last year, rated good year on year.
points.so_what: Cancellations remain better than last year even after this week's deterioration against the prior week.

points.what: New signups fell to 251, down 3.1% on last week and down 3.1% on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Signups moved down while orders rose 4.5%, so the two are no longer moving in the same direction.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
